# CD cell and row finalization

`cd_finalization_mathjax_3_2_2.json` stores 1,813 complete SVG strings from
D2's frozen MathJax 3.2.2 bundle, upstream commit
`ad8f5c21cb810236551da8c6512ba733e67357ee`. The fixture records the three
original asset hashes. Every case uses a fresh VM and the unmodified D2
conversion with `em=16`, `ex=8`, no font cache, and the recorded display mode.
No SVG values are normalized or generated by the Go implementation.

The primary source is
[`AmsCdMethods.arrow` and `cell`](https://github.com/mathjax/MathJax-src/blob/ad8f5c21cb810236551da8c6512ba733e67357ee/ts/input/tex/amscd/AmsCdMethods.ts),
with `EndEntry`, `EndRow`, and `EndTable` in
[`ArrayItem`](https://github.com/mathjax/MathJax-src/blob/ad8f5c21cb810236551da8c6512ba733e67357ee/ts/input/tex/base/BaseItems.ts).
They define three distinct boundaries:

- An `@` arrow closes preceding content, pads empty cells to the proper
  alternating column, and closes the arrow cell. `cell` reads the actual
  stack top: an ArrayItem receives a strut in its first object cell, while
  pending items have no table or row properties and receive the same strut
  even in later columns and arrow rows. The strut arrives before active
  styles, positions, functions, and infix denominators finish.
- A row separator closes the pending cell even when it is empty. It does
  not insert a CD strut.
- The environment ending closes a pending cell only when nodes or previously
  closed cells remain. A final no-node row is omitted; a real leaf `mspace`
  or explicit empty group is retained.

SetFont changes the environment without adding a stack item. A pending
FunctionItem therefore stays on the same row when a font declaration arrives,
just like pending Prime, Not, Dots, and Position items. Retaining that item
allows the later CD strut, StyleItem, or other successor to reduce it in the
source order. Genuine child parsers, groups, and fences do not inherit the
synthetic CD closing boundary.

The corpus covers plain and arrow-closed rows, leading and trailing arrows,
adjacent arrows, omitted objects, horizontal and vertical labels, equality
and dot arrows, empty rows, trailing separators, explicit empty objects,
spaces, no-node declarations, comments, groups, colors, ten math sizes,
pending parser items, and grouped nested CD diagrams. It also composes CD
with fractions, roots, scripts, fences, boxes, text, and ordinary matrices.
Additional controls exercise every pending item in the first and later
columns and in arrow rows, single Braket/Set owners, and generic font/function
continuations outside CD. There are 1,775 valid renderings and 38 matching
error controls. Against the base-strut baseline `fc0dc08787d16dd7f6a2aa56e91210b541753acb`,
1,055 references fail and 758 controls already match. All 1,813 match after
the fix.

A visible public witness is
`\begin{CD}A@>f>>B\\@VgVV@VVhV\\C@>>k>D\\\end{CD}`:
the old parser emits an extra final row, enlarging the diagram and shifting
its baseline. `\begin{CD}A@>>>\Huge x@>>>B\end{CD}` also shows why a pending
style receives the strut in a later column before the cell closes.

## Historical residual inventory and current followups

`cd_finalization_residuals.json` preserves the raw inputs and complete
original, baseline, and candidate outputs for all 123 separately identified
residuals in the wider 1,934-case audit: 81 valid original expressions and
42 malformed-input diagnostic differences. The report records validity,
whether candidate output changed from the baseline, and whether the baseline
was exact. None was formerly exact. It also hashes the two production source
files used for the observation. After composing this fix with the base-strut
fix, the two missing-strut cases became byte-exact. Their original SVGs are now
also asserted in the primary corpus, leaving 121 unresolved cases (79 valid
and 42 diagnostics). The historical observations remain intact.

- The two missing base `\strut` cases are now resolved by the preceding
  base-strut fix and this CD correction. Four explicit CD ampersand cases still
  require a cell-splitting fix.
- Six nested-environment/arrow-scanning and `\cr` row-splitting cases are
  byte-unchanged. In particular, an outer matrix currently splits an inner
  CD's row separator before finding its `\end{CD}`.
- Ten ordinary `@` cases now have the correct cell boundaries and dimensions,
  but Base `Other` still lacks the original ORD `TeXAtom` wrapper. The raw
  candidate output changed; the original reference remains preserved.
- One indexed-root display case now has the correct CD tree and geometry
  except an existing viewBox rounding tie (`-2755.7` versus `-2755.8`). Its
  candidate output changed. The inline form is an exact passing control.
- Eighteen additional valid CD compositions retain separate parser/layout
  gaps: the environment's blanket arrow-minimum rewrite affects authored
  `xrightarrow`; raw CD preprocessing intercepts `@` before an unbraced
  fraction argument can consume it; and completed Braket/infix compositions
  have existing mismatches. Four changed through other repaired CD boundaries.
- Forty valid generic font/infix and single-Braket continuations retain
  existing composition mismatches outside the CD closing boundary; 24 changed
  after preserving FunctionItem across font declarations. The raw references
  and candidate observations remain available for the next focused fixes.
- Forty-two malformed-input diagnostics remain byte-unchanged from baseline.

These cases are reported separately rather than changing original receipts
or representing qualified comparisons as exact matches.

Regenerate both sets of original references with
`node --jitless testdata/generate_cd_finalization.cjs PINNED_ASSETS`.
The generator uses subprocess batches of 24 fresh VMs to bound Node's memory
use while keeping every expression isolated.
Run `go test ./... -run TestCDFinalizationReferences`.
